item3_dual_client.status: CORE OBSERVED on the real authenticated transport; not yet against a spawned Runner/child process

delivered.outbound_channel: business-channel.ts now owns BOTH directions: the Runner's inbound waiters and its outbound callbacks (fact, payload-read, native-write-intent), all scoped to the lease generation that created them
delivered.routes: GET /v1/channel/next hands the lease the next callback, POST /v1/channel/reply routes one reply to the request it names. Both sit behind the existing bearer auth; the producer is the authenticated one and the lease id only scopes waiter ownership, so it grants nothing
delivered.runner_service: the three callbacks ask the bound lease first and fall back to stdio when no client is attached, so the product lane is unaffected
delivered.detach: a different lease replaces the current one: pending native writes become state_indeterminate / write_indeterminate_after_detach, outbound callbacks of the old lease are dropped, and the old client's later reply is refused
delivered.no_replay: no business command is replayed and no permission migrates on rebind; the caller must return to the original command reconciliation

cases: B27-DUAL-A-SERVES-ALL-THREE - A served the fact receipt by its original id and the payload by its original ref
B27-DUAL-PENDING-WRITE-INDETERMINATE-ON-LEAVE - the pending native write became write_indeterminate_after_detach when B took the lease, so B was never asked to grant it
B27-DUAL-A-REPLY-REFUSED-AFTER-HANDOVER - a reply from the old client was refused after the handover
B27-DUAL-B-SERVES-NEW-FACTS-BY-ORIGINAL-ID - B served the fact for the new lease using the original fact id
B27-DUAL-FACTS-REPLAYED-TO-B - B replayed both original facts by their original ids from the same Runner

item4_sigkill.status: CORE OBSERVED on a real spawned Runner with a real OS-level SIGKILL
item4_sigkill.design: the Runner is spawned once and publishes its own endpoint; coordinator A is a separate OS process that reads the original attempt and leaves a registration; A is killed with SIGKILL; coordinator B is a different PID that reads only that registration and resumes
cases: B27-SIGKILL-RUNNER-REGISTERED - the Runner published a pinned endpoint that outlives its coordinators
B27-SIGKILL-COORDINATOR-A-OBSERVES - coordinator A read the original attempt and epoch with the original fact ids
B27-SIGKILL-COORDINATOR-A-DIED - coordinator A died by SIGKILL while the Runner kept running
B27-SIGKILL-NEW-PID-RESUMES-SAME-REGISTRATION - a new PID resumed the same attempt and epoch and re-read the same original fact ids
B27-SIGKILL-BEGIN-WINDOW-NOT-REPLAYED - re-feeding begin with its original id was refused as duplicate_begin instead of replayed
B27-SIGKILL-DELIVER-KEEPS-ORIGINAL-ID - re-feeding deliver with its original id was accepted, so the id was not replaced by a fresh one

defectFixed.genericRefusalMessage: the transport collapsed every non-200 into 'Runner recovery request was refused or indeterminate', so a duplicate_begin refusal was indistinguishable from an unknown outcome. The transport now carries the server's own error code, and the command route returns the admission's code/reason as a structured 409 instead of letting a rejection become a generic failure
